summary: Switzerland is not in the EU but joins the Schengen Area through association agreements: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, nationals of the countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (Annex II of Regulation 2018/1806) can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (the ETIAS travel authorization is not yet in operation), and everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa (general fee €90).

roadVignette.text: Switzerland sells exactly one vignette: CHF 40, valid for 14 months from December 1 of the previous year to January 31 of the following one. There are no short-term options, so a single motorway trip costs the full CHF 40. You can choose the e-vignette linked to your number plate or the sticker on the windscreen; both cost the same. Only at Basel St. Louis, Rheinfelden and Kreuzlingen may you use the motorway without one, and only as far as the first exit.

tips.text: The 90-day limit counts stays across the whole Schengen Area, not only in Switzerland.

Driving on Swiss motorways requires a vignette (CHF 40, as a sticker or e-vignette). The UK FCDO says you can buy one at most border crossings, petrol stations, post offices or online, and that driving without one can bring a large fine; Canada notes rental cars are generally equipped with one.

faq.question: Is Switzerland in the EU or the Schengen Area?
faq.answer: Switzerland is not an EU member, but it is part of the Schengen Area through association agreements, so the same short-stay visa rules apply as in the EU Schengen states. For goods, the UK FCDO says there are strict rules about what you can take into and out of Switzerland, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Switzerland?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can visit Switzerland and the rest of the Schengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS starts, they will need to obtain this online authorization (€20) before travel.

faq.question: How much does a Switzerland Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The general Schengen short-stay visa fee is €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11; children under 6 pay nothing. Where the application goes through an external service provider, as at most Swiss representations, its service fee is added. The visa allows stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries.

faq.question: Do I have to declare cash when entering Switzerland?
faq.answer: There is no obligation to declare cash on entry. However, if you carry CHF 10,000 or more (or equivalent), customs officers can require you to disclose your identity and the origin, intended use and beneficial owner of the money — refusing or lying is a customs offense.

faq.question: Do I need a vignette to drive in Switzerland?
faq.answer: Yes — using Swiss motorways requires a vignette costing CHF 40, valid for 14 months (1 December of the previous year to 31 January of the following year), available as a windscreen sticker or an e-vignette registered to your plate. Driving on a motorway without one incurs a CHF 200 fine, and you must buy the vignette on the spot as well.
